messages:
Maya Chen: Quick heads-up: we need to pick a clear Q plan for Sequencing vs. Batching. Customers are pushing for batching but infra warns on p95.
Jules Park: Can we quantify the tradeoffs? I want concrete RICE inputs rather than gut.
Samir Patel: From telemetry: batching would cut token spend for top-tier customers ~15-20%. But worst-case p95 could increase 20-30% for small-window workloads.
Ana Ortiz: Enterprise risk is realthey expect SLA parity. Even small tail regressions have churn risk.
Leo Zhang: Implementation notes: batching touches KV cache semantics and routing. Effort estimate = 3 months; sequencing controls are mostly feature flags + rollout logic = 2-3 weeks.
Jules Park: Proposed RICE parameters: Reach (% orgs affected): batching=35, sequencing=55. Impact (0-10): batching=7, sequencing=4. Confidence: batching=0.55, sequencing=0.8. Effort (months): batching=3, sequencing=0.25.
Samir Patel: Quick math: batching = (35*7*0.55)/3 = 44.9; sequencing = (55*4*0.8)/0.25 = 704. Huge diff because sequencing effort is tiny.
Ana Ortiz: RICE is favoring low-effort wins; but we should layer in strategic value and potential revenue protection for batching. Maybe cap sequencing scope to avoid masking the underlying cost issue.
Maya Chen: Recommendation: prioritize sequencing this quarter to reduce release friction and enable experiments, but fund a one-sprint P0 spike for batching focused on latency de-risking and targeted pilot commits.
Jules Park: Agree. Add strict launch criteria for batching: - p95 regression <= 10% on Dedicated setups OR - adaptive-routing fallback reduces client-visible p95 within 200ms for 95% of requests.
Samir Patel: I'll design the spike: perf harness across models, KV-flush scenarios, different seq lengths, and stress tests. Results due in 1 sprint.
Ana Ortiz: CS will recruit two pilot customers on Dedicated for an opt-in batching trial and capture success metrics: cost delta, p95, and product KPIs.
Leo Zhang: I'll break sequencing into smaller tickets: feature flags, telemetry, canary rollout path. Estimate: 2 engineers, 3 weeks.
release-bot: Canary pipeline created: canary/sequencing-toggle. Playbook: https://internal.runbook/sequencing-canary
Maya Chen: Action items: Jules update the roadmap card with RICE and decision; Samir owns spike plan; Ana owns pilot outreach; Leo owns sequencing tickets + rollout. Check-in next Thurs.
Jules Park: Putting notes on the roadmap board and pinging stakeholders. :thumbsup:
Ana Ortiz: CS owners added and initial pilot emails sent.
Samir Patel: Perf harness scheduled Wed-Thu next week.
Leo Zhang: Tickets created: PROD-8620, PROD-8621.
Maya Chen: Thanks team. We'll treat batching as a measurable outcome we only escalate if the spike and pilots validate. Next sync to confirm go/no-go for Dedicated pilot.
